symptom: peeing a lot more often for months
hook: the whole kidney had turned into a lump of chalk
whatYouSee: The left kidney is replaced by a dense lump of chalky calcium that still keeps a rough kidney shape.
whyItMatters: This is the classic picture of end-stage tuberculosis of the kidney. The destroyed kidney calcifies into a nonfunctioning mass called a putty kidney. Classic clues are urinary frequency and sterile pyuria.
treatment: Standard antituberculous therapy treats the infection. A painful or infected nonfunctioning kidney may be removed by nephrectomy.
takeaway: A chalky nonfunctioning kidney with a putty texture is tuberculous autonephrectomy.

findings: Frontal abdominal radiograph, apparently AP supine or semi-erect, with the lower chest, full lumbar spine and pelvis included.

Large clustered mass of dense, granular, popcorn-like radiopacities in the left upper abdomen, in the expected gastric or splenic flexure region, with a lobulated outline and mottled internal texture.
Air-fluid level or gas bubble in the gastric fundus at the left upper quadrant, suggesting an upright or semi-upright position; the gastric lumen appears otherwise opacified or soft-tissue dense.
Multiple air-filled loops of bowel in both lower quadrants with haustral pattern; no definite marked dilatation.
Right renal outline appears as a smooth oval soft-tissue density; no obvious calculus is seen on it.
Linear thin lines crossing the abdomen obliquely, likely skin folds, gown or clothing artifacts or tubing.
Vertebral column is straight with no obvious fracture; the pelvis is symmetric, and the sacroiliac joints and hips are grossly unremarkable.
Image is slightly rotated, with some beam-hardening and edge vignetting artifact.
differential: Ingested radiopaque material (pills, concretions or foreign bodies) aggregated in the stomach or bowel, such as a pharmacobezoar or ingested heavy-metal or iron tablets
Gastric bezoar with calcific or contrast-coated content
Residual oral contrast or barium within a bowel loop or diverticulum
anatomyConcerns: The dense granular cluster is unusually discrete and sharply marginated for normal bowel content and does not match a normal organ calcification pattern, so it is likely extrinsic or ingested material rather than native anatomy.
Its position relative to the gas bubble suggests intragastric or proximal colonic location, but this cannot be confirmed on a single projection.
Oblique linear lines are acquisition or clothing artifacts, not anatomic structures.
No impossible anatomy identified; the left kidney is not clearly seen, likely obscured by bowel gas and the dense material.

clueFacts.clue: peeing a lot more often for months
clueFacts.fact: In renal tuberculosis, urinary frequency over months can occur because infection often spreads to the bladder, where inflammation and a shrunken, irritable bladder wall reduce capacity.
